title: SUPER CHEAPO
text:
SUPER CHEAPO. You get what you pay for. Sadly in this case, it's even less. I missed the part that described this a COMPLETELY particle board with a cardboard back. (That's right, I thought it was packing. Nope, the folded cardboard in the packing mix was to be used as the backing of the dresser). The laminate paper is SO thin that if just look at too long it will rub off. Honestly, If I hadn't had to destroy the box to get it out (SUPER HEAVY) I would have just returned it. I think the seller is hoping you won't. Good thing Amazon backs up what they sell.

PROS:
*It was packaged about as well as I have ever seen. The edges were super reinforced. I've never seen such a well packaged cardboard box. (Having said that, the top piece was still broken in several places - sigh)
*It was packaged securely inside as well.
*I am 53, female. Put it together, by myself, in about 4 hours.
*Most of the pre-drilled areas were correcting drilled.
*Had all of the screws/parts needed, but see below..
*It's stylish... sort of retro looking to me.
*Honestly, it looked like a daunting task. But once started, it went fairly quickly.
*Ording from Amazon. They (Amazon) are SUPER good at coming up with solutions.

CONS:
*Upon taking inventory of all the misc screws and parts, I discovered one of the carpentry screws was broken. Sadly, the local hardware store did not carry them. Neither did the local furniture store. Contacted the manufacturer, NO RETURN CALL.
*NO SELLER CUSTOMER SERVICE AT ALL. Calling the 800 number gets you voice mail that they apparently don't ever pick up or return.
*This is such a cheap piece of furniture, it's hard to believe they could sell them for more than a $100. I will use it only temporarily and then it will likely go to the dump.
*The directions have NO written instructions. Pictures are good but did NOT help with the screws that were different than those packed WITH the handles. Eventually I sorted it out. But printed instructions would have helped there.
*As cheap as this dresser is, I was really disappointed to see that one of the drawer liner laminate was "flawed" right in the center. I put that drawer on the bottom row, but it is still an eyesore.
*The top was broken is several places, three showing on the top piece of the dresser. Again, I attempted to contact the seller thinking I might be able to purchase or obtain a new top piece. Seller does NOT RETURN PHONE CALLS OR ANY CONTACT.
*Smell. It smells like the chemicals used in making particle boarding. I believe there is a study that says those chemicals are harmful. Another reason it will most likely end up in the dump.

If you're still thinking you might try it, here's what you will need to make it easier:
A small hammer, a cordless drill (that you can easily control), a flat head and phillips screw driver. About 4-5 hours, maybe less if you have a second set of hands.
Optional: A shot of whiskey for the frustration factor.

Hope this is helpful in some way.

UPDATE: 5/18 Dresser on the way to the dump. Purchased a very nice drawer, on sale, at the local furniture store. Can't say I'm sad to see it go. I think the lesson here is that in regards to furniture, perhaps it's better to purchase locally so you can actually see and approve of what you're getting. Happy shopping!
